name: Rhinoplasty simulation apps

lead: Rhinoplasty simulation software lets a person or a surgeon alter a photo or 3D scan of a nose to show a proposed change. The payoff is seeing a preview of the result immediately and having a clearer plan for nose surgery.

Surgical references describe 3D simulations and 3D cameras that capture and analyse the nose, allow modifications, and help surgeon and patient understand the anatomy. Consumer apps that morph a photo exist alongside clinical systems. The topic appears in looksmaxxing discussion as a way to preview a result before surgery.

paras: Software maps the nose from standard photographs or 3D camera captures and lets the operator reshape contours digitally. Clinics use it in consultations so patient and surgeon can align expectations, and consumer apps offer similar photo morphing.

The tools themselves are low-risk. The surgical result can differ from a simulation because healing, swelling and tissue behaviour vary between individuals; swelling after rhinoplasty can take a year or more to fully settle.

angle.text: Clinics and prospective patients use morphing and 3D imaging software to preview how a nose might look after surgery and to align expectations with the surgeon. The preview image is visible immediately. The actual surgical outcome can differ from it.

lead: Rhinoplasty simulation apps and software let people preview how a nose might look after surgery, or after different changes to its shape, by editing a photo or a 3D model. The point is to see a proposed profile or tip before committing, and to give surgeon and patient a shared picture of the target.

Surgical references describe 3D simulations and planning that can communicate the patient's existing deformities and the planned approach, and 3D cameras that capture, inspect, analyse and modify the nose so a potential result can be shown to the patient.

Clinical systems of this kind sit alongside consumer apps that morph a photo. They belong to the wider field of computer-aided surgical simulation, in which specialized software renders a virtual 3D model of the patient and simulates intervention before surgery [1].
infobox: Photos from several angles or a 3D camera capture

paras: Rhinoplasty references describe software-based 3D simulation as a way to show existing deformities and plan the proposed approach, and 3D cameras as a way to inspect the nose and edit it virtually so both parties can discuss a likely outcome.
Pre-operative consultation also includes a history, an exam of skin type, symmetry, valves and septum, and photographs from several angles, which supply the images these tools work from.

Healing differs between people and swelling can take at least a year to fully diminish, which is relevant to how closely a preview resembles a final result. Wikipedia cites revision surgery as needed in roughly 5 to 20 percent of rhinoplasties, while flagging that the article needs more citations.

Wikipedia describes the general approach as using specialized software to render a patient's gathered data as a virtual 3D model, with surgical intervention simulated before surgery. It cites maxillofacial examples such as bone segment navigation in orthognathic surgery and mid-face reconstruction; it does not address cosmetic nose previews specifically [1].
